examples.question_text:
Two triangles have sides $6$ cm and $5$ cm. The angle opposite the $5$ cm side is $30^{\circ}$.
Find both possible values of the angle $\theta$ opposite the $6$ cm side, correct to the nearest degree.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{\sin\theta}{6}&=\dfrac{\sin30^{\circ}}{5}\\\sin\theta&=\dfrac{6\sin30^{\circ}}{5}=0.6\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}(0.6)\approx36.8699^{\circ}\\\theta'&=180^{\circ}-\theta\approx143.1301^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$143.1301^{\circ}+30^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$, so both angles are valid.

$\theta\approx37^{\circ}$ or $143^{\circ}$.

examples.question_text:
A triangle has sides $4$ cm and $10$ cm. The angle opposite the $10$ cm side is $30^{\circ}$.
Find the angle $\theta$ opposite the $4$ cm side, correct to the nearest degree.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{\sin\theta}{4}&=\dfrac{\sin30^{\circ}}{10}\\\sin\theta&=\dfrac{4\sin30^{\circ}}{10}=0.2\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}(0.2)\approx11.5370^{\circ}\\\theta'&=180^{\circ}-\theta\approx168.4630^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$168.4630^{\circ}+30^{\circ}>180^{\circ}$, so the obtuse partner is rejected.

$\theta\approx12^{\circ}$ only.

examples.question_text:
A triangle has sides $5$ cm and $10$ cm. The angle opposite the $10$ cm side is $120^{\circ}$.
Find the angle $\theta$ opposite the $5$ cm side, correct to the nearest degree.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{\sin\theta}{5}&=\dfrac{\sin120^{\circ}}{10}\\\sin\theta&=\dfrac{5\sin120^{\circ}}{10}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5\sin120^{\circ}}{10}\right)\approx25.6589^{\circ}\\\theta'&=180^{\circ}-\theta\approx154.3411^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$154.3411^{\circ}+120^{\circ}>180^{\circ}$, so the obtuse partner is rejected.

$25.6589^{\circ}+120^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$, so the acute angle is valid.

$\theta\approx26^{\circ}$ only.

examples.question_text:
A triangle is claimed to have sides $9$ cm and $4$ cm. The angle opposite the $4$ cm side is $30^{\circ}$.
Try to find the angle $\theta$ opposite the $9$ cm side and explain why the triangle is impossible.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{\sin\theta}{9}&=\dfrac{\sin30^{\circ}}{4}\\\sin\theta&=\dfrac{9\sin30^{\circ}}{4}=1.125\end{aligned}$

Since $\sin\theta$ cannot exceed $1$, no such triangle exists.

examples.question_text:
In triangle $PQR$, $p=7$ cm, $q=10$ cm and $\angle P=30^{\circ}$.
Find both possible sizes of $\angle Q$, correct to the nearest degree, and the corresponding lengths of side $r$, correct to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{\sin Q}{10}&=\dfrac{\sin30^{\circ}}{7}\\\sin Q&=\dfrac{10\sin30^{\circ}}{7}=\dfrac57\\Q_1&=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac57\right)\approx45.5847^{\circ}\\Q_2&=180^{\circ}-Q_1\approx134.4153^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$134.4153^{\circ}+30^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$, so both angles are valid.

Keep the calculator values for the side calculations.

$\begin{aligned}R_1&=180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}-Q_1\approx104.4153^{\circ}\\r_1&=\dfrac{7\sin R_1}{\sin30^{\circ}}\approx13.5592\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}R_2&=180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}-Q_2\approx15.5847^{\circ}\\r_2&=\dfrac{7\sin R_2}{\sin30^{\circ}}\approx3.7613\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

The possibilities are $Q\approx46^{\circ}$ with $r\approx13.6$ cm, or $Q\approx134^{\circ}$ with $r\approx3.8$ cm.

examples.derivation: sin(theta)=6 sin(30°)/5=0.6. The angles are 36.86989765° and 143.13010235°. Both leave a positive third angle with the given 30°, giving 37° or 143°.
sin(theta)=4 sin(30°)/10=0.2. The candidates are 11.53695903° and 168.46304097°. The latter plus 30° exceeds 180°, leaving 12° only.
sin(theta)=5 sin(120°)/10=sqrt(3)/4. The candidates are 25.65890627° and 154.34109373°. Only the first fits alongside 120°, giving 26°.
sin(theta)=9 sin(30°)/4=1.125. This exceeds the maximum sine value of 1, so no such triangle exists.

sin(Q)=10 sin(30°)/7=5/7, giving Q1=45.58469140° and Q2=134.41530860°. Both are valid. The remaining angles are 104.41530860° and 15.58469140°. Applying the sine rule gives r1=13.55923352 cm and r2=3.76127455 cm, confirming the paired results (46°, 13.6 cm) and (134°, 3.8 cm).
